explanation:
## What the grid is made of

Every input has a background of 7 and a few solid rectangles. Each rectangle has exactly one corner cell replaced by an 8. Here are the cases from the fact sheet:

- **Pair 1:** the 9-block (0,0)–(1,1) has its 8 at (1,1), the bottom-right corner. The 1-block (1,5)–(4,7) has its 8 at (1,5), the top-left. The 5-block (6,1)–(9,5) has its 8 at (6,5), the top-right.
- **Pair 2:** the 2-block (1,1)–(5,5) has its 8 at (1,5), the top-right. The 6-block (7,5)–(8,8) has its 8 at (7,5), the top-left.
- **Pair 3:** the 2-block has its 8 at the bottom-right. The 9-block has its 8 at the bottom-right. The 3-block has its 8 at the bottom-left.

The 8 is not adjacent to only one colour. In pair 3, the 8 at (5,9) touches both 9 and 3. So I do not attach each 8 by adjacency. Instead I take each colour's bounding box and check which of its four corners holds an 8.

## How the output is built

In the outputs every 8 has disappeared. Each rectangle is filled solid with its own colour, and it has moved one cell diagonally toward the corner where its 8 was.

- **Pair 1:**
  - 9 had its 8 at the bottom-right and moved from (0,0)–(1,1) to (1,1)–(2,2).
  - 1 had its 8 at the top-left and moved from (1,5)–(4,7) to (0,4)–(3,6).
  - 5 had its 8 at the top-right and moved from (6,1)–(9,5) to (5,2)–(8,6).
- **Pair 2:**
  - 2 moved up-right to (0,2)–(4,6).
  - 6 moved up-left to (6,4)–(7,7).
- **Pair 3:**
  - 2 moved down-right to (4,1)–(7,4).
  - 9 moved down-right to (3,8)–(6,10).
  - 3 moved down-left to (7,7)–(9,9).

Pair 3 shows why the order of work matters. The new 9 rectangle covers row 6, where the 3-block used to be. So I first erase every old object, including the 8s, and then paint every moved rectangle onto the clean background. No two rectangles overlap in any output, so the painting order does not matter.

## Applying it to the test

| Colour | Bounding box | 8 at | Corner | Shift | New box |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | (0,0)–(4,2) | (4,2) | bottom-right | (+1,+1) | (1,1)–(5,3) |
| 3 | (0,8)–(2,10) | (2,8) | bottom-left | (+1,−1) | (1,7)–(3,9) |
| 4 | (3,4)–(6,5) | (3,5) | top-right | (−1,+1) | (2,5)–(5,6) |
| 2 | (6,6)–(7,7) | (7,7) | bottom-right | (+1,+1) | (7,7)–(8,8) |

None of these new boxes overlap.

## Program

The program emits two teaching stages: the canvas with all objects erased, and the final canvas after painting the moved rectangles.

movement.text: | Colour | Bounding box | 8 at | Corner | Shift | New box |
Repaint each rectangle solid, shifted one step diagonally toward the corner its 8 marked.
